subject: pink meanie jellyfish
title: This Jellyfish Has 70-Foot Tentacles and Only Hunts Other Jellyfish

scenes.text: This jellyfish hunts the one prey nobody expects.
The pink meanie can top 50 pounds, with tentacles up to 70 feet long.
Scientists spotted it in the Gulf of Mexico around 2000 and mistook it for a known species.
DNA later proved it belonged to an entirely different family of jellyfish.
Its prey? Moon jellyfish. It snares them in those tentacles and digests several at once.
When the moon jellies vanish, pink meanies die off fast. A jellyfish that lives on jellyfish.

description:
The pink meanie is a jellyfish that hunts other jellyfish.
It can weigh more than 50 pounds with tentacles up to 70 feet long, feeds mainly on moon jellyfish, and turned out to belong to a whole separate family when DNA tests came in.
Would you want to swim into one of these?
first_comment: Young pink meanies start out eating plankton like other jellyfish; only the big ones switch to hunting moon jellies. Which would you rather meet: a pink meanie or a box jellyfish?
